Hi all — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise engineering plan and recommended headers. I attached a short "observability-hooks.md" and an SDK auth patch (sdk-auth-sample.patch) for quick testing.

1) Trace propagation
- Recommendation: support both W3C TraceContext (traceparent) for compatibility with existing tracing systems and a dedicated header X-Redwood-Trace for quick lookups. We set X-Redwood-Trace = <redwood-trace-id> (UUID) on inbound request and propagate it unchanged to model runners, and include it in logs. Example: X-Redwood-Trace: 4f47a2b8-8d6e-4c7a-9b2f-2b9f8a7e6c2a
- For fan-out / async work: include the original X-Redwood-Trace in the message payload/headers for your workers. If a new trace is required by a downstream system, include traceparent for span-level trace while keeping X-Redwood-Trace for correlation.
- Retries: each retry is annotated with retry count in the logs and carries the same X-Redwood-Trace. We also add X-Redwood-Retry: 1 (numeric).

2) Latency breakdown headers (response headers)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Total: total end-to-end ms (integer)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Model: model runtime ms (integer)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Queue: queuing/batching delay ms (integer)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Network: network overhead ms (integer)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Cache-Hit: boolean string (true/false) when prefix cache avoided model run

These are placed on the final HTTP response and are suitable for ingestion into your API gateway logs (we recommend sampling full JSON traces for problematic requests).

3) Auth patterns & SDK support
- Short-lived keys: we support a token exchange flow (client-credentials -> short-lived API token with TTL). SDKs include helper to refresh tokens automatically. See attached sdk-auth-sample.patch for a minimal implementation.
- mTLS: for Private deployments we support client cert auth at the front door and can map cert identity to service account. If you prefer mTLS we can provision a CA-signed cert for your staging pool.
- OAuth: we support client-credentials; we can provide an example OAuth flow you can plug into your identity provider (Auth0/Okta).

4) Embeddings + reranker guidance
- Low-latency path: store vectors in your vector DB (we recommend Faiss/Weaviate/Pinecone) and call Redwood only for reranking to keep cost down. Reranker cost is proportional to candidate count; typical pattern: top-100 candidates -> rerank.
- Simpler path (less infra): call Redwood for both embedding and rerank, but note additional latency and cost. We can provide a quantized embedding model for lower cost.

5) SDK & observability examples (attached)
- Attached observability-hooks.md contains: concrete response headers, log fields we emit (redwood.trace_id, redwood.model_name, redwood.batch_size, redwood.token_count, redwood.latency_ms), and an example dashboard query for your Grafana/Datadog.
- Example HTTP response (from Redwood):
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  X-Redwood-Trace: 4f47a2b8-8d6e-4c7a-9b2f-2b9f8a7e6c2a
  traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
  X-Redwood-Latency-Total: 124
  X-Redwood-Latency-Model: 98
  X-Redwood-Latency-Queue: 18
  X-Redwood-Latency-Network: 8
  X-Redwood-Latency-Cache-Hit: false

6) Next steps / timeline
- We can provide a 30-min engineering sync with your infra (we're available Wed 8/12 10:00 PT or Thu 8/13 9:00 PT).
- Action items for FintechCo: provision a staging API key (scoped) or provide mTLS cert for staging; share an internal contact for vector DB questions.
- We'll drop the attached observability-hooks.md and a tiny SDK patch for token refresh in the repo for you to try.

If you want, we can also add a small tracing middleware you can deploy in your gateway to rewrite/ensure X-Redwood-Trace is present.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the example.

— Dev
